item.title: depression
item.description:
what do i know?
  1. i am experiencing a period of acute depression.
    it is likely triggered by the breakup with a, but caused by more than that.
  2. it’s exhausting, oppressive, and painful.
  3. it feels like it’s been going on for a very long time.
  4. sometimes there are periods (~4-24+ hours) where it feels untolerable.
    it is unclear to me what triggers these specific periods.
  5. i’ve struggled with chronic depression in the past, and will continue to do so.
  6. it feels like this reaction is outsized to the breakup.
  7. i am in therapy, and i meet with a psych NP.
  8. the episodes are unpredictable, and highly disruptive to my life.
    this is frustrating.
  9. i’ve experienced feelings like this before, to this severity, and i have gotten better.

why is this happening, and why now?
  1. unclear, honestly
  2. other contributing factors:
  • i don’t have a good support system, or a community to rely on
  • i feel very alone, and very lonely
  • i live alone
  • things are work were tumultuous; i almost rage quit a few times.
  • i felt very purposeless and unanchored
  • a had provided: an anchor, a deep sense of companionship and comfort of being myself, affection, laughter, stimulation, and the inroads towards a friends and a community that i liked

how are things now?
  1. i still do not many friends whom i love being around, and who bring me joy and laughter and a sense of fun and companionship, in new york. i am still very alone.
  2. things are shifting at work.
  3. prior / in-midst of the disruption i was thinking about:
  • getting tango shoes, and trying tango more deliberately
  • possibly getting more involved with the queer tango crew
  • a life direction; a career change – things have moved a bit more here
  • working through my apartment (shelving, cleaning, rearranging, reducing down– )

many of these things are still relevant. it feels – a little more clear.

item.title: signs
item.description:
a,

everything i see in the universe, i see as a sign.
as you had said to me, i over-interpret everything that happens.
so.
we choose not to misinterpret, now.
i interpret to nothing. i close the door on meaning, and sit down, my back against the door, and only hope to feel you on the other side.

last night i read the article you assigned the reading club, even though i will choose not to attend. it was wonderful. prescient; human; surprisingly full of gentleness — it had been a long while since something lit up my brain in the same way, sent so many zingles of sparks shooting off in different directions i barely had time to catch their trails. i wrote to you then.

item.title: things i have learned
item.description:
things I have learned:

  1. i can fall in love with someone in less than 7 days
  2. physical affection, especially if gentle and genuine, overrides everything else.
  3. i am like a moth to a light to a fascinating mind. better if their wanderings are weird - paths i have never encountered before, and continue to not be able to conceive of. better even, yet, if they have the a loving, kind, painfully generous heart.
  4. (addendum to above) this is strange, because i don’t think i’m this myself, especially my mind. unclear if i’d ever find a match, be good enough for the kind i’d like.
  5. still, there exists people out there for whom my desires fit like a key to a lock – who, astoundingly, want the same things I want: who pulls me closer in to them, all the time; who asks if they can carry me to bed; who, once there, falls in the same spell as i do into his; who teases me; who makes me laugh; who comes back, again, and again, and again
  6. if c was found by sheer luck; a by a stone’s toss; then surely it must follow that there will be others out there;
  7. i wish to be more alive in the way that they are - thinking, being, engaging with the world, laughing, playing, joy, so present
  8. a is an excellent writer
  9. a is a weirdo
  10. even when it’s clear that it’s not something that they want, or it’s something that they’re conflicted about, men seem to have a harder time calling it off, and then I have to do it for them.
  11. i am terrible at it, too.
